clips.title: No one knows how when they begin — ideas don't come out fully formed
clips.why: Removes the exact excuse the scared 22-year-old is holding: 'I haven't had my big idea yet, I don't know enough to start.' A billionaire saying 'let me tell you a secret, no one does when they begin' and 'if I had to know everything first I never would have built Facebook' takes that excuse away and leaves something startable tonight. Three separate replay peaks sit on these lines — viewers rewound here.

clips.title: You're sure someone else is going to do it — but they're not. You will.
clips.why: The build is short and the payoff is a direct hit on the viewer's passivity: 'it never even occurred to me that that someone might be us, we were just college kids... I just assumed one of them would do it.' Then the turn to camera — a change in the world that seems so clear that you're sure someone else will do it, 'but they're not, you will.' Kills the 'someone smarter is already on it' excuse with a story that proves it.

clips.text: I remember that night I launched Facebook from that little dorm in Kirkland house I went to noes with my friend KX and I remember telling him clearly that I was excited to help connect the Harvard Community but one day someone would connect the whole world the thing is it never even occurred to me that that someone might be us we were just college kids we didn't know anything about that there were all these great big technology companies with all these resources and I just assumed one of them would do it but this idea was so clear to us that all people want to connect so we just kept working on it day after day after day and I know that a lot of you are going to have your own stories just like this a change in the world that seems so clear that you are sure someone else is going to do it but they're not you will but it's not enough to have that purpose yourself you also have to create a sense of purpose for others and I found that out the hard

clips.title: Can I really do this? The student who had every reason to be cynical
clips.why: Opens on the exact question the viewer is asking — 'maybe you're asking yourself, can I really do this?' — and answers it with a story: an undocumented teenager who may be denied his dream, who instead of feeling sorry for himself asks for a book on social justice for his birthday. 'He has every reason to be cynical... but he wasn't feeling sorry for himself.' The landing hands the courage back to the viewer. Six replay peaks mark this story. It runs long (~100s) but the build is doing real work and every beat earns its place; a later pass can narrow it.

clips.title: Be prepared to be misunderstood
clips.why: Names an experience the ambitious viewer has already lived and never had explained: called crazy for a big vision, blamed for not understanding the problem, criticized for moving too fast. The rhythm of 'anyone who... is going to...' makes it feel like a law of nature rather than comfort, and the close — 'that can't stop us from getting started' — converts it into fuel.

near_misses.why_not: 'I know too many people who didn't have a cushion to fall back on' is honest and names a real humiliation, but the message is 'success needs luck and money' — it removes self-blame yet leaves the viewer with no handhold. Direction check is shaky for this category.

The impostor confession — 'I wondered if I was just wrong, an impostor, a 22-year-old kid' — lands hard, but the resolution ('that is how things work when there's no sense of higher purpose') is about company-building, and the pain-to-turn ratio is off for a standalone reel.

The prayer he sings to his daughter and 'I hope you find the courage to make your life a blessing' is genuinely moving and heavily replayed, but it is comfort and blessing rather than a change in how the viewer sees themselves — likely the emotional finder's material.
The JFK janitor story and 'purpose is being part of something bigger than yourself' is well-made commencement material but the viewer's brain has filtered this sentence shape a thousand times.

That's where the material for the 2am scroller lives.
